title: EMC English Conversation Club
description:
**EMC English Conversation Club**
**Thursdays, 4 to 6pm**
**Free.** Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

Whether you want to improve your English or you're a native speaker keen to help others, this is a great place to connect and build friendships.
This is not a classroom. It’s a relaxed community space where you can share stories, practise everyday English, and learn about life, work, and culture in New Zealand and other countries.
Each session is guided by an experienced facilitator and supported by friendly volunteers.
**What to expect:**
• Casual, friendly conversations on real-life topics
• Supportive facilitators and volunteers
• Language learning through connection, not pressure
• A welcoming environment to build friendships and confidence

Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

title: 🌏 Auckland Asian Networking Night
description:
Looking to meet new people, expand your professional network, or simply enjoy meaningful conversations over a drink?

Auckland Asian Networking Night is a relaxed community meetup inspired by Auckland's diverse Asian community, bringing together people from all backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and build genuine relationships.

You don't have to be Asian to join. If you enjoy meeting people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate Asian cultures, you're more than welcome.

No presentations. No formal agenda. Just good conversations.

👥 WHO'S THIS FOR?
Whether you're:

* A professional from any industry
* An entrepreneur or small business owner
* A freelancer or creative
* A student or working holiday maker
* Looking for a new career opportunity
* Or simply interested in meeting new people

💬 WHAT TO EXPECT
Grab a drink, introduce yourself, and join any conversation that interests you.

There's no fixed seating, no scheduled activities, and no pressure. Simply move around, meet different people, and enjoy conversations at your own pace.

You might leave with:

* New friends
* Professional connections
* Career insights
* Business opportunities
* Collaboration ideas
* Or simply a great evening with interesting people

Most people attend on their own, so don't worry if you're coming solo. We'll help you feel welcome.

📍 EVENT DETAILS

* Location: Mixed 1981 Cafe, 50 Fort St, Auckland CBD, Auckland
* Time: 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM (feel free to arrive a little earlier to grab a drink)
* Frequency: Every two weeks
* Capacity: Limited spaces available
* Entry: $10 per person, FREE for Hanahub members (Free to sign up at [hanahub.co.nz](https://www.hanahub.co.nz/))

☕ This event is proudly sponsored by Mixed 1981. All attendees are required to purchase at least one drink, and Hanahub members enjoy a drink discount, so simply show your profile on the night.

🍪 Korean snacks will be served on the night, so come and enjoy a taste of Korea while you mingle.

🎒 WHAT TO BRING

description:

Join us for another Hack The Box meetup in Auckland! Whether you're thinking about being a hacker or are already a seasoned one, this event has something for everyone.

title: Building, Instrumenting & Scaling Production Agentic AI
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

We're excited to invite you to the August **Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup**!

This month, we are diving deep into productionizing agentic AI systems—from instrumenting serverless deployments for rapid debugging to scaling resilient agentic architectures under real-world enterprise load. We are thrilled to host two fantastic speakers!

We are gathering once again at the Pushpay office in the CBD—looking forward to seeing you all there!

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/auckland-aws-tools-and-programming-meetup-aug-26-building-ai-agents/register)**

**🎤 The Lineup**
**Darshit Pandya (Senior Principal Engineer, Platform Engineering @ Serko)**

* **Title:** Strands Agents on Lambda: Observability With Powertools & X-Ray
* **Description:** When a Strands Agent fails across five Lambda log streams with no correlation, debugging takes a minimum of 20 minutes. This session demonstrates a structured observability layer that reduces diagnosis to under two minutes. You'll learn how Lambda Powertools Tracer wraps Strands tool invocations as X-Ray subsegments, how Powertools Logger injects AgentCore session correlation IDs across invocations, and how Powertools Metrics surfaces tool retry frequency as CloudWatch alarms — before timeouts occur. The session covers three production failure classes: tool timeout, reasoning loop, and retry storm, and provides a reusable CDK construct that provides full instrumentation for any Strands Agent Lambda deployment.

#### **Geethika Guruge (Principal Consultant @ Mantel)**

* **Title:** From Timeout to Throughput: Scaling Resilient Agentic Systems
* **Description:** Moving an AI agent from prototype to production requires more than optimism. This session tackles the "Day 2" engineering challenges of scaling

title: Demystifying Git
description:
**Topic**
Many of us use git for our day to day work, but do we really know whats going on? Today we will peek under the hood and get an idea of how git works under the covers. By understanding some of the git internals, we will be better equipped to recover when things go wrong (hello merge hell). No matter if you’re a beginner or an expert, there will be something you can use to improve your workflow.

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please use the following link to pre-register for Xero Venue before arriving** [https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S](https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S).
* **Organisers will be at the building entrance to bring everyone to the venue.**
* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: Shipping software as a Junior without burning out by Enry Villamizar**
Stepping into software engineering is exciting, but navigating the steep learning curve alongside deliverable deadlines can easily lead to early-career fatigue. In this talk, you will learn actionable strategies for shipping production-ready code confidently without sacrificing well-being. From setting clear boundaries and managing workload expectations to building sustainable dev habits.

**A bit about Enry:**

* Enry is a Senior Software Developer driven by solving real-world business problems through smart internal software, such as building Whites Powersports’ warehouse system and Wireless Nation’s dashboard. A huge fan of video games and AI, he cares deeply about keeping development work sustainable, efficient, and burnout-free.

**Talk 2: Beyond the Prompt: Becoming a Better Developer in the Age of AI by Keith Patton**
AI tools can help junior developers produce working code faster than ever, but speed is not the same as engineering competence.
In this talk, he will share practical lessons from using AI coding tools and agentic development workflows in real software teams. He will cover where AI is genuinely useful, where it can create false confidence, and how developers can use it without outsourcing their understanding or judgement.
